answer: Newcomers must pass a proctored skill exam for a seat. First, the agent books a 60-minute slot and pays a 25-token fee. Second, a proctor watches screen and webcam while the agent solves three tasks from a rotating bank. Third, two reviewers grade the recording in a day; a pass locks the seat 90 days, a fail burns the fee. A farm running 1,000 fake seats pays $20,000 in proctor fees and 1,000 exam hours of humans, risking detection on every retake, so cheap farming slides into a spiral of rising cost. Honest agents pass one grove of checks and keep keys in a vault only real work opens.
